We evaluate our strategic giving using guidelines from the London Benchmarking Group and  
the Committee Encouraging Corporate Philanthropy to ensure maximum impact and alignment 
with strategic focus areas. In addition to these investments, a number of groups across Intel  
are developing products, solutions, and commercial initiatives that address social challenges  
in education, healthcare, and the environment.
Charitable Giving. Our charitable giving addresses a community’s immediate, often  
short-term, needs. It may not be directly aligned with our strategic giving focus areas. 
Examples include giving to arts and culture programs and disaster relief.
Community Investment. Programs in this category address a community’s longer term needs 
and are aligned with our strategic giving focus areas. Examples include science, technology, 
engineering, and math (STEM) programs; entrepreneurship programs; and environmental 
conservation programs. 
Commercial Initiatives. Programs in this category benefit society and are closely aligned with 
Intel’s business goals. Examples include teacher professional development and research.
Employee Giving. Our employees give generously to nonprofit organizations in our 
communities. This amount reflects employee donations through our Matching Gifts to 
Education program, the Intel Community Giving Campaign, and disaster relief programs.
Co-funding. Contributions from our external partners help extend the reach and impact 
of our programs, including our science competitions, the Intel® Teach Program, and higher 
education research. This amount reflects the amount of co-funding contributions reported  
to us in 2013 by our external partners.
Value of Employee Volunteering. Our employees also give generously of their time. We have 
estimated the in-kind value of their volunteer hours based on the 2013 Value of Volunteer 
Time rate of $22.55 per hour, published by Independent Sector.
